loop.top3_why: The mean combination (full pool) shows the most stable performance across the three validation windows (0.6727, 0.6545, 0.6364) and is less sensitive to the unstable model ranking indicated in the diagnosis. It also aligns with the dataset‑wide observation that plain mean performs robustly on trend‑dominated series. The dba strategy, while having the lowest overall score, exhibits a growing error across windows, suggesting possible over‑fitting to early windows. The weighted inverse‑error strategy spikes dramatically in the last window, reflecting high variance in weight estimation with only three windows. Therefore, the plain mean offers the best balance of stability and robustness for this series.
loop.top3_why_not: A (dba) has the best raw score but its error rises steadily across windows, indicating it may be over‑fitting to the early validation period. C (weighted inverse error) performs well in the first two windows but its error explodes in the third, showing high sensitivity to the limited weight‑estimation data and unstable ranking. Both are less robust than the plain mean given the trend‑dominated, highly predictable nature of the series and the diagnosis of unstable model ranking.
